title: per-tenant-kv-leaseback-and-staged-fallback-for-cache-heavy-paths
creator: Maya Alvarez
description:
Problem: During regional surges we see disproportionate tail-latency and connection saturation on Redis clusters and stateful cache sharded stores. Current all-or-nothing fallback strategies (full cache bypass -> DB reads) cause downstream DB amplification and tenant-level outages.

Goal: Implement a per-tenant leaseback + staged fallback system for KV-backed read paths that: (1) prevents connection pool exhaustion by progressive admission and session-aware throttling, (2) preserves soft-cached responses via leaseback reads when shard latency spikes, (3) gracefully degrades tenants with configurable profiles rather than global bypass, and (4) integrates with existing circuit-breaker/hysteresis controls and multi-region failover policies.

Success metrics (SLO-driven):
- Reduce Redis-originated connection errors by 60% under 2x baseline traffic bursts.
- Prevent >90% of tenants from elevated downstream DB read amplification during a cache degradation event.
- Keep P99 end-to-end latency for high-priority tenants within 2x baseline during partial-degrade scenarios.

Scope: server-runtime admission controllers, tenant-profile configs, leaseback protocol (read-with-lease → cached fallback), staggered degrade policies, integration with console rollouts/alerting, and end-to-end tests (chaos + load). Not in scope: full redesign of the KV protocol or changing shard placement logic.

Design summary:
1) Tenant profile: each tenant has a configurable degrade profile (priority, burst-tolerance, DB-protect flag, preferred-fallback-region).
2) Session-aware admission controller: token-bucket per-session + per-tenant soft-quotas; when pool pressure crosses thresholds, controller applies progressive throttling tiers (soft-shed → prioritized-hedge → leaseback-read → circuit-open for non-critical traffic).
3) Leaseback read: when a direct cache read exceeds latency threshold or pool queue is backed up, the runtime attempts a lightweight leaseback read (serve cached metadata or last-known-good value from a local ephem cache + background refresh) with a short TTL to avoid stale critical writes.
4) Staged fallback: fallback pathways escalate in stages with hysteresis windows — 1) local ephem cache, 2) stale-while-revalidate (serve then refresh), 3) routed read to remote read-only replica in another region, 4) fallthrough to DB for tenants explicitly allowed (DB-protect flag prevents this).
5) Circuit-breaker integration: per-tenant circuit metrics (error rate, lat_p99 of dependency, queue-depth) drive automatic transitions and alerting. Configurable annealing/backoff and manual override via Console.

Outcomes & trade-offs:
- Pro: reduces blast radius by targeting tenants and sessions; prevents immediate DB amplification; offers predictable SLA tiers.
- Con: added runtime complexity and more tenant configuration surface; requires operational visibility to tune profiles and TTLs; slight risk of serving slightly-stale values in edge cases (controlled via DB-protect flag).

Operational plan: Start with canary rollout to 10% of traffic for low-risk tenants in us-west, monitor key metrics, then expand. Implement robust dashboards (per-tenant connection errors, fallback ladder counts, leaseback hit ratio, DB-read amplification) and set automated rollback conditions.

Docs & artifacts: Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Per-Tenant+Leaseback+Design (internal). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9983 (runtime admission controller).
comments: 2025-01-11 — Maya Alvarez: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Agreed to keep DB-protect as opt-in for tenants with strict consistency needs. Jordan to prototype admission controller. (ref: drive/leaseback/proto).

2025-01-20 — Jordan Patel: Prototype admission controller implemented. Early results: local ephem cache reduced synchronous Redis calls by ~22% under synthetic burst. Profiling shows additional 8% CPU overhead at peak. Draft PR opened: runtime/pull/9959.

2025-01-28 — Priya Mehta (SRE): Reviewed canary plan. Requested explicit rollback SLI thresholds: >5% increase in DB RPS sustained for 5m OR >3x P99 increase for critical tenants -> automatic unblock and rollback. Added to runbook.

2025-02-03 — Design feedback (Ezra King): Suggested tightening lease TTL window for write-heavy tenants and creating a tenant opt-out for stale-serving. Added tenant flag: stale_serve_allowed=false. Updated design doc.

2025-02-09 — Jordan Patel: End-to-end chaos test (region failover + connection exhaustion) completed in staging. Observations: staged fallback prevented DB amplification for 92% of simulated tenants; however, under extreme cross-region latency the leaseback refreshes queued up, causing transient CPU spikes. Added backpressure to leaseback refresh worker. See test logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/leaseback/chaos/2025-02-09.
2025-02-12 — Maya Alvarez: Marking In Progress -> continuing iterations. Next: telemetry dashboards (ENG-1100460) and controlled canary to 10% traffic on us-west by 2025-02-20.
